candidates.change: `sp_capacity: CapacityInKilobytes(256) -> CapacityInKilobytes(128)`. Scratchpad SRAM 16,384 → 8,192 rows (2,048/bank across sp_banks=4; power of two, multiple of DIM=16). The `SparseCraftZBU` bitmap is elaborated with n = rows-per-bank, so its flat register file halves from 4,096 to 2,048 bits per bank without any RTL edit. No ZBU or PE logic changed.

candidates.rationale: live working set is 3,328 rows (2,048 X-resident + 256 A + 1,024 B) of 16,384 — 80% of the scratchpad macro is powered, leaked and area-charged holding nothing, and the ZBU bitmap is elaborated with n = rows/bank so it halves with it (16,384 → 8,192 flops) along with the 4,096:1 mux on the read-enable path.

candidates.change: delete the T-A2 accumulator-input hold (`held_c` + mux, outputType=20b per PE), keep the 8-bit `in_a` hold
candidates.rationale: iteration 3 measured the whole gate at +69,754 µm² (~272 µm²/PE), and ~28 of those flops per PE are the 20-bit psum hold, which only quiesces the final adder while the 8-bit hold already quiesces the 8×8 multiplier — the expensive half of the gate buys the cheap half of the MAC.

T-B taps mvin only, so the accumulator's Y read-modify-write sweeps are untouched inside the ~20.6 µJ on-chip remainder; a 4× longer acc-resident K-pass cuts those sweeps 4×, and it needs no elaboration.
